about: Inkling 2 Mini (26B looped MoE, ~3B active, vision, thinking) UD-IQ4_XS with the F16 vision projector on one 24 GB card: the full 262,144-token window with a q8_0 KV cache, no draft model. Unsloth's llama.cpp prebuilt mix with unslothai/llama.cpp#386 at 7db4a706, which lets a quantized KV cache use the banded relative-bias attention kernel; before it, a quantized cache made llama.cpp build a dense bias of rows x context x 24 heads (5.1 GiB at 256K with -ub 128), and 256K fit only with q4_0 KV at -ub 32. -ub 128, backend sampling (-bs), the vision projector on the CPU (about 2 s for a small image) to leave room for the cache, one slot, Thinking Machines' recommended sampling. On an RTX 3090 that also drove a desktop (about 1.7 GB), the whole card peaked at 22,016 MiB over the gates, and at 22,588 MiB with a 250,000-token context followed by short requests of 21 to 35 new tokens (the dense-bias case). host_ram_gb is the measured fall in MemAvailable (2.4 GB at start, 2.2 GB over the gates), rounded up. Decode falls with context: about 58 tok/s near empty, 28 tok/s at 250,000 tokens.
install: Unsloth's llama.cpp prebuilt mix, built from source for sm_86 with unslothai/llama.cpp#386 at its CUDA quantized K/V commit: git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp llama.cpp-unsloth && git -C llama.cpp-unsloth checkout b12606, then git merge --no-ff, in listed order, every PR commit pinned in https://github.com/unslothai/llama.cpp/blob/b1c7f862c98fdb919caeaf1200ccd9cf0af8424c/scripts/unsloth/pr-set.json, taking #386 at 7db4a7064afffe7fbed81227473182559d227222 instead of 242a5d8f, and resolving add/add conflicts with that repo's scripts/unsloth/additive_merge.py as its unsloth-prebuilt.yml does (merged tree 79eb8746aa1ffeabbe228788a6343e5f37a7bddd); then cmake -S llama.cpp-unsloth -B llama.cpp-unsloth/build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86 -DGGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON -DGGML_CUDA_NCCL=OFF -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DLLAMA_OPENSSL=OFF && cmake --build llama.cpp-unsloth/build -j --target llama-server (CUDA 13 toolkit; we built in nvidia/cuda:13.3.1-devel-ubuntu22.04 with GCC 11.4)
setup: Not Docker; Linux x86-64 with an NVIDIA driver for CUDA 13. Build llama.cpp-unsloth/ as in install, next to models/, and run from that directory (building inside the nvidia/cuda:13.3.1-devel-ubuntu22.04 image works too). If the CUDA 13 runtime is not on the library path, put libcudart.so.13, libcublas.so.13 and libcublasLt.so.13 in cuda13-runtime/ (for example from NVIDIA's cuda_cudart 13.3 and libcublas 13 redistributables). The launch uses most of a 24 GB card; close other GPU programs first.
